title: Power adders and swaps
notes: 22 fact cards. facts/WP-17.md did not exist on disk at run time (ledger showed WP-17 status todo), so no sibling ECU-tuning file to cross-check against; this WP stuck to power-ADDER hardware and swaps only. Section A (turbo/supercharger kits, F-WP18-001..010): confirmed exactly 3 real, brand-named, GD3-specific kits ever sold -- KraftWerks/Jackson Racing Rotrex-supercharger kit and HKS's CARB-EO'd (D-186-27, directly read from the EO record itself, Tier 2) bolt-on turbo kit, both independently confirmed DISCONTINUED (absent from both brands' own current shop catalogs, read directly), plus Unequal Fabrication's current small-fabricator 'GD3 (07-08) Turbo Kit' ($2,300, shown out-of-stock/made-to-order, not confirmed discontinued). One D8 near-miss caught and excluded: a well-written DrivingLine.com turbo-Fit feature article was directly read and found, in its own text, to name the GE8's L15A7 engine, not this book's L15A1 -- discarded entirely (F-WP18-010) rather than used with a caveat. Section B (engine swaps, F-WP18-011..018): exactly ONE engine family documented as actually swapped into a GD3 -- Honda K-series (K24A2, K20Z3) -- via 2 independent named build sources (pbomers.com's detailed build page; a 2014 k20a.org thread, cross-corroborated by a second forum reply and a 2022 rarity-discussion thread) plus 3 independent retailers (Hybrid Racing/King Motorsports/RPM Racing) all stocking the same Hasport GD-swap mount kit as commercial market evidence. Key obstacles documented in detail: motor mounts (Hasport or reinforced stock), front-core-support cutting for intake clearance, hand-built wiring using an 07-08 Acura TSX ECU (Hondata/KTuner) plus immobilizer resync, transmission swap (08 Civic Si w/ LSD -- K24 transmission casings explicitly do NOT fit), 02-04 RSX-base axles, an EP3 power-steering idler arm, and a custom exhaust header. Total swap cost left honestly UNVERIFIED (no source gave a total; only a $249-285 mount-kit component price was found); rarity estimated informally by one community member at 'less than 50 done worldwide' -- not a real count. No B-series/D-series/H-series/non-Honda/EV-motor swap into a GD3 was found as a completed documented build (only a same-forum discussion thread and a same-forum question thread for each) -- reported honestly as few-to-no documented examples per the task's own instruction, not invented. A speculative 'King Motorsports SEMA K24 Fit' claim surfaced by an early AI search summary was directly checked and could NOT be corroborated -- rejected, not used (F-WP18-016). Section C (fuel/clutch/axle, F-WP18-019..022): Exedy Stage 1 (128 ft-lb, part 08807, $454) and Stage 2 (160 ft-lb, part 08954) clutch kits confirmed GD3-specific via a direct-read retailer listing plus independent FitFreak corroboration of the same torque figures; stock clutch reported (community, single-search-pass, low confidence) to slip under boost, motivating the upgrade. Fuel: 410cc RDX injectors reported used with the KraftWerks kit at 10psi (Hondata forum), Walbro/Deatschwerks 255lph pumps reported used for custom turbo builds (FitFreak) -- both WebSearch-snippet-only (hondata.com and fitfreak.net both Cloudflare-blocked to curl and r.jina.ai this pass, consistent with every prior WP). Axle/driveshaft: NO source found reporting stock CV axles need upgrading specifically because of added power (as opposed to ordinary wear/corrosion, already WP-02's subject, or the K-swap's unrelated axle-spline-compatibility issue) -- left honestly UNVERIFIED (F-WP18-022) rather than assumed. 2 conflicts logged to queue/conflicts.md: C-017 (two different KraftWerks kit power figures, 121 vs 164 whp, likely two product tiers but not confirmed) and C-018 (an unverified eBay '485HP' marketing claim vs. a real 160-260 whp community consensus for GD3 turbo builds -- eBay claim rejected, not used as a fact). 11 new WP-scoped source cards added (S-WP18-A through S-WP18-N, some letters skipped where a source was WebSearch-snippet-only and not formally carded per plan Section 3). Bottom line for the calling task: exactly 3 real branded turbo/supercharger kits (2 discontinued, 1 currently out-of-stock-but-listed) and exactly 1 engine family (K-series) with 2 independently-sourced documented swaps -- genuinely thin, niche territory, honestly reported as such rather than padded.

title: Fuse and relay maps
notes: 3 fuse boxes documented (interior behind driver's coin tray, primary under-hood on driver's side, secondary 80A fuse on battery positive terminal) with all 33 interior + 16 under-hood + 1 secondary fuse positions (50 total), each with amperage and circuit, as two clean markdown tables. All from a direct read of the real 2008 Fit Owner's Manual PDF (S-001, techinfo.honda.com via r.jina.ai per ADAPT-2), whose fuse-chart OCR came through jumbled (numbers/amps/circuit-names as separate runs, not a laid-out table) but was reconstructed position-by-position and cross-checked token-for-token against a new Tier 3 source (S-WP21-A, fuse-box.info GD 2007-2008 page) with an exact match on every position -- 0 discrepancies, 0 conflicts logged. Also covered: fuse puller location (interior fuse box), the 5-step check-for-blown-fuse procedure, and the safety-critical 'never replace with a higher-rated fuse' + 'repeat blow = see a qualified technician' guidance, both quoted directly from the manual per D9. 1 UNVERIFIED fact (F-WP21-015): the manual documents fuses only, no separate relay map/box diagram was found anywhere in it despite the WP title 'fuse and relay maps' -- flagged as a gap, not invented. Note: fuse table position 18 is genuinely equipment-dependent in the manual itself (TPMS if equipped vs. Canadian-model DRL), recorded as such (F-WP21-014) rather than picking one value.
